title: Weston's Two Chefs Wins South West Chef Honour at National Curry Awards
excerpt: Two Chefs Indian Restaurant of Weston-super-Mare was named South West Chef of the Year at the ARTA 2026 Grand Finale in London, after a live national cook-off against chefs from 15 UK regions.
body:
• Two Chefs Indian Restaurant of Weston-super-Mare won South West Chef of the Year at the Asian Restaurant and Takeaway Awards (ARTA) 2026.
  • Winners were announced at the Grand Finale on October 12 at the London Hilton on Park Lane, hosted by Samantha Simmonds and Paul Sinha.
  • More than 1,250 businesses across the UK were nominated for ARTA 2026, and Two Chefs also reached the South West regional restaurant shortlist.
  • Two Chefs earned its place through a live national cook-off at Cambridge Regional College, where chefs from 15 UK regions competed.

A Weston-super-Mare Indian restaurant has taken a regional title at one of British Asian hospitality's biggest national awards nights. Two Chefs Indian Restaurant was named South West Chef of the Year at the Asian Restaurant and Takeaway Awards (ARTA) 2026, with the winners announced at the Grand Finale ceremony on October 12 at the London Hilton on Park Lane, according to the awards' published winners list on SSZEE Media.

The ceremony, hosted by TV news anchor Samantha Simmonds and comedian Paul Sinha, brought together restaurateurs, chefs and hospitality professionals from across the country. Guests included actor and dancer Lauren Gottlieb, singer and former Lok Sabha member Hans Raj Hans, and Paul Waugh MP. More than 1,250 businesses across the UK were nominated for this year's awards.

How Two Chefs Got There: The Cook-Off

The chef titles were not decided on reputation alone. Two Chefs represented the South West in the ARTA 2026 National Chef of the Year cook-off, a live competition held at Cambridge Regional College that brought together chefs from 15 regions of the UK, selected following more than 1,200 nominations nationwide, That's Food and Drink reported.

Competitors cooked from an extensive choice of fresh ingredients, including king prawns, rack of lamb, chicken, sea bream, seasonal vegetables, pulses, herbs and spices. Judges assessed hygiene, technique, creativity, use of ingredients, presentation, flavour, texture, appearance and aroma. The judging panel drew on culinary educators, experienced restaurateurs and professional chefs from Cambridge Regional College and the wider hospitality industry, and students from the college prepared and served lobster for competitors and guests.

Two Chefs had also been shortlisted in the Regional Restaurant of the Year category for the South West, a ten-strong list that included restaurants in Bristol, Poole, Torquay, Taunton and Bath. That regional restaurant title ultimately went to Bombil of Bristol, while the national Chef of the Year crown went to Kusturi Indian Restaurant of Colchester and the Champion of Champions award to My Delhi Newcastle.

A Big Night for Asian Hospitality

ARTA, now in its seventh year, is widely described as the "Oscars of the Curry Industry." Its judging takes in food and service quality, value for money, hygiene standards and customer feedback posted through Google and Tripadvisor. Founder Mohammed Munim used this year's ceremony to underline what the sector contributes beyond the dining room.

"This industry represents far more than food."

— Mohammed Munim, Founder and CEO, ARTA

Munim described Asian restaurants and takeaways as an integral part of multicultural Britain, supporting communities and creating employment, while noting that the sector is absorbing rising employment costs, food prices and energy bills. ChefOnline was the strategic partner for ARTA 2026, with Cambridge Regional College as skills partner.

What It Means for Weston

For a seaside town better known nationally for its pier than its dining scene, a South West chef title puts Weston-super-Mare on the same results sheet as London, Birmingham and Newcastle. For diaspora readers in the South West, the practical takeaway is straightforward: an award-winning Indian kitchen, validated through a live judged cook-off rather than a popularity vote alone, is operating in Weston-super-Mare, and the full ARTA 2026 winners list doubles as a usable shortlist of regional restaurants worth trying across the UK.

Two Chefs returns home with the regional chef crown while the restaurant category honours went elsewhere, which sets up next year's question: whether the kitchen can convert a chef title into a regional restaurant title at ARTA 2027.
